title: Graceful-degrade routing lanes: percentile-aware routing with soft regional quotas and emergency shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: During regional load spikes and partial outages we need a deterministic way to route requests that preserves latency SLOs for critical customers while avoiding noisy failovers that cause cross-region cascade. This ticket proposes a lanes-based routing controller that assigns requests to latency lanes (fast, best-effort, emergency) using percentile signals, soft regional quotas, and progressive circuit-breaking preemption to shed work before downstream queues overload. The goal is graceful degradation with observable cutover points and simple rollback semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Controller routes by observed P50/P95/P99 latency bands and respects soft regional capacity quotas
When a region crosses a configured circuit-breaker (latency or queue-growth), new requests are moved to a degradation lane or overflow region according to policy instead of immediate global failover
Load-shedding paths are bounded and prioritized: critical API keys and SLO-tagged customers remain in higher lanes until their dedicated quotas are exhausted
Metrics emitted: per-lane QPS, dropped requests, latency percentiles per region/lane, circuit-breaker state transitions; dashboards and alerts added

Canary rollout exercised against a shadow traffic slice and validated with chaos test that simulates partial region outage without violating overall global 99th percentile SLO beyond a configurable budget
design_notes:
High level:
1) Lanes: fast (low-latency), steady (throughput-optimized), and emergency (best-effort / shed). Each incoming request is assigned a lane based on (a) request priority (SLO-tag/plan), (b) client latency tolerance header, and (c) current lane occupancy and latency percentiles for candidate regions.
2) Percentile signals: use a short-window sliding quantile (30s/2m) to compute P50/P95/P99 and smoothed derivative to detect growing latency. Thresholds configurable per-region.
3) Soft regional quotas: each tenant (or API-key class) has weighted quota tokens per region. The router prefers home region until the tenant's soft quota is near exhaustion, then routes to next-best region while preserving lane semantics.
4) Progressive circuit-breaker: multi-phase CB with increasing scope — phase 0: local lane demotion (fast -> steady), phase 1: soft reject to emergency lane, phase 2: reject with 429 for non-critical classes and open external failover only for critical classes. TTI (time-to-intervene) hysteresis with exponential backoff.
5) Preemption & pre-emptive shedding: when a region shows sustained queue growth, controller will preempt best-effort requests and reassign to other regions or emergency lane. Preemption respects per-tenant quotas and max cross-region burst budget.
6) Telemetry: enrich tracing with lane, region-choice-reason, CB-state, and quota-remaining. Expose per-tenant and per-region budgets via Console.

Implementation sketch:
- Router module extension: lane assignment engine + quota evaluator + percentile signal consumer (from runtime metrics stream)
- New lightweight policy language (JSON) for per-project lane rules (priority thresholds, fallback order, quota weights)
- Circuit-breaker state machine implemented in router control-plane with authoritative state replicated via existing config-store

Trade-offs considered:
- Immediate failover is simplest but causes flash congestion in target regions; lanes reduce cascade but add routing complexity and more telemetry.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit tests and integration tests for lane assignment and CB transitions
2) Deploy to staging and run synthetic load to exercise lane demotion and preemption logic
3) Canary: enable controller for 1% of production traffic (non-paying tenants) with shadowing to validate decisions
4) 10% rollout with traffic shaping and close SRE watch; validate dashboards and alarms
5) Gradual ramp to 100% with automated kill-switch to revert routing to current stable policy
6) Post-rollout: run chaos experiments that simulate region flaps and verify bounded SLO impact
metrics_and_alerts: Emit metrics: router.lane.assignment{region,lane}, router.quota.remaining{tenant,region}, router.cb.state{region}, router.dropped.total{tenant,reason}. Alerts: - router.cb.entered for any region > 3 transitions in 5m - lane.drop-rate > 0.5% for critical tenant class - cross-region-burst > configured budget. Dashboard: lane heatmap by region + per-tenant quota burn chart. Tie alerts to on-call SRE + PM channel.
